court: Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit

issues.label: Appellate jurisdiction under §1252
issues.why: The court must confirm it has jurisdiction to review the final order and any limits on review.

issues.label: Final agency action identity
issues.why: The court must determine whether the BIA adopted the IJ and what reasoning constitutes the reviewable decision.

issues.label: Issue exhaustion before BIA
issues.why: The court must decide whether each argument was properly raised to the BIA as a prerequisite to judicial review.

issues.label: Claim exhaustion before IJ
issues.why: The court must assess whether PSGs or theories first raised on appeal were forfeited for not being presented to the IJ.

issues.label: Standard of review
issues.why: The court must apply substantial-evidence review to fact findings and de novo review to legal questions.

issues.label: Preservation of political opinion claim
issues.why: The court must determine whether the political-opinion theory was preserved and properly presented for review.

issues.label: Political opinion cognizability
issues.why: The court must decide whether “opposition to violence/rule of law” can qualify as a protected political opinion.

issues.label: Actual political opinion held
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether the record compels a finding that petitioner genuinely held the asserted political opinion.

issues.label: Imputed political opinion
issues.why: The court must consider whether the persecutor attributed a political opinion to petitioner even if she did not hold it.

issues.label: Political opinion nexus
issues.why: The court must decide whether threats were “on account of” actual or imputed political opinion versus personal retaliation.

issues.label: Past persecution threshold
issues.why: The court must determine whether threats and related harm rise to the legal level of past persecution.

issues.label: Future persecution objective reasonableness
issues.why: The court must decide whether the feared harm is objectively reasonable given the record.

issues.label: Persecutor identity and motive
issues.why: The court must assess whether the feared persecutor is the father, his associates, or others and their motivations.

issues.label: Government inability or unwillingness
issues.why: For asylum/withholding, the court must determine whether El Salvador is unable or unwilling to protect her from private actors.

issues.label: Internal relocation feasibility
issues.why: The court must consider whether safe and reasonable relocation within El Salvador defeats a well-founded fear.

issues.label: Particular social group framework
issues.why: The court must ensure each PSG meets immutability, particularity, and social distinction requirements.

issues.label: PSG: females viewed as property
issues.why: The court must decide whether this PSG is legally cognizable and supported by record evidence.

issues.label: PSG: Salvadoran women
issues.why: The court must decide whether this PSG is cognizable and, if raised late, whether it was waived/forfeited.

issues.label: PSG: nuclear family of Porfiria
issues.why: The court must decide whether this family-based PSG is cognizable and properly defined.

issues.label: Family-based PSG nexus
issues.why: The court must determine whether harm was motivated by familial ties to Porfiria rather than retaliation for accusations.

issues.label: PSG: family of prosecutorial witnesses
issues.why: The court must determine whether petitioner was a member of this PSG and whether it was properly preserved.

issues.label: PSG: family of witnesses to crime
issues.why: The court must decide whether this newly framed PSG is barred as unexhausted/forfeited and, if not, its merits.

issues.label: Membership in proposed PSGs
issues.why: The court must assess whether the record compels a finding that petitioner fits each claimed group.

issues.label: Nexus ‘one central reason’
issues.why: The court must apply the statutory nexus standard for asylum to determine whether a protected ground was a central reason.

issues.label: Mixed-motive analysis
issues.why: The court must consider whether protected-ground motives coexisted with personal motives and whether nexus still exists.

issues.label: Withholding nexus standard
issues.why: The court must apply the different nexus standard for INA withholding (protected ground as “a reason”).

issues.label: Asylum burden and eligibility
issues.why: The court must determine whether petitioner met the burden for asylum (past persecution presumption or well-founded fear).

issues.label: Asylum discretionary denial
issues.why: If eligibility is found, the court must consider whether any discretionary factors were at issue or require remand.

issues.label: Withholding probability standard
issues.why: The court must decide whether petitioner showed a clear probability of persecution if removed.

issues.label: Derivative asylum eligibility
issues.why: The court must verify J.P.A.’s derivative status requirements and dependency on the principal’s asylum outcome.

issues.label: Derivative limitations for withholding/CAT
issues.why: The court must recognize that withholding/CAT do not confer derivative benefits and assess any separate entitlement.

issues.label: CAT definition of torture
issues.why: The court must determine whether feared harm qualifies as “torture” (severity and intent) rather than lesser mistreatment.

issues.label: CAT likelihood standard
issues.why: The court must decide whether it is more likely than not petitioner would be tortured on return.

issues.label: CAT actor requirement
issues.why: The court must assess whether torture would be by, at the instigation of, or with consent/acquiescence of officials.

issues.label: Government acquiescence test
issues.why: The court must apply the correct standard for acquiescence (including willful blindness) to police inaction or corruption.

issues.label: CAT evidence of official involvement
issues.why: The court must evaluate record evidence about the murder investigation and whether non-prosecution implies acquiescence.

issues.label: CAT country conditions relevance
issues.why: The court must consider whether country conditions evidence corroborates risk and official complicity/ineffectiveness.

issues.label: CAT internal relocation relevance
issues.why: The court must consider whether relocation affects the likelihood of torture (not as a strict bar but as a factor).

issues.label: Credibility and corroboration
issues.why: Although credibility was found, the court must ensure no legal error occurred regarding corroboration expectations or weighing evidence.

issues.label: BIA’s treatment of new PSGs
issues.why: The court must decide whether the BIA properly declined to reach PSGs raised for the first time on appeal.

issues.label: Reasoned decisionmaking
issues.why: The court must determine whether the IJ/BIA adequately considered material evidence and explained conclusions.

issues.label: Substantial-evidence support
issues.why: The court must decide whether the record compels reversal of key findings on nexus, persecution, and acquiescence.

issues.label: Legal error vs factual dispute
issues.why: The court must distinguish reviewable legal errors (wrong standards) from unreviewable or deferential fact determinations.

issues.label: Remand scope if error found
issues.why: If reversible error exists, the court must decide which issues require remand to the agency for further findings.
